chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, a man from the Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Advise me.' So, among what he advised him with was that he said: 'Do not insult the people, lest you acquire enmity between them.'

key_terms.بَنِي تَمِيمٍ: Banu Tamim, a prominent Arab tribe

ai.seo_question: What advice did the Prophet give to the man from Banu Tamim regarding social conduct?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) traces the Prophet’s advice to a Banu Tamili man, emphasizing that verbal insults are not merely personal offenses but catalysts for broader social discord. In Shia scholarly tradition, this underscores the concept of 'adab al-kalam' (etiquette of speech), where maintaining communal harmony is a direct consequence of avoiding the accumulation of enmity through careless words.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man from the Clan of Tameym came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and he said, ‘Advise me’. So, among what he<sup>saww</sup> advised him with was that he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not insult the people for it would earn you the enmity between them’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from abu Basir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Once a man from the people of Tamim came to the Holy Prophet and said, ‘Instruct me with good advice.’ Of the good advice given to him was: ‘Do not revile people; it only earns their animosity against you.’”
